title: StackServiceFile
description:
One service's file, `services/<id>.toml`: exactly one `[[service]]`, whose `id` is
the name the file is filed under, and nothing else.

Bind.description: Which interface a service's port is published on.

Claim.description:
The core capability a plugin claims, and the probes it is demonstrated by.

The vocabulary owns what must be shown; this owns where to ask. A capability is
one contract with many claimants, each answering at a path of its own, so the
published probe declares the question and the statuses that answer it, and the
binding declares the method, the path and the recorded response.

capability.description: A core name, which must also appear in the service's `provides`.

probe.description: One binding per probe the capability declares. Every one of them, exactly once.

ClaimProbe.description:
One probe of a claimed capability, bound to a request on this plugin's service or,
where the vocabulary declares the probe a run, to a run of its image's own program.

expect.description: What the answer must be, within what the probe permits.

fixture.description:
The recorded response.

Required here where it is optional on a proof: a claim nobody can demonstrate
without owning the service is a claim the catalogue's own checks cannot make.

id.description: Names a probe the capability declares.

request.description:
Method and path on this plugin's own service. Exactly one of this and `run`, and
this where the vocabulary declares the probe a request.

run.description:
Arguments to the image's own entrypoint, run with no network. Exactly one of this
and `request`, and this where the vocabulary declares the probe a run.

Criticality.description:
How much a service's absence costs.

Serialisable as well as readable, because it reaches an operator: a status
report that says a service is down without saying whether that matters
leaves them to guess, and the manifest already holds the answer.

oneOf.description: Its failure has consequences outside the machine.
The form does not work without it.

Dashboard.description: A service's entry on the household's dashboard, where its wiring names any of it.

icon.description: The icon it shows, from the dashboard's own icon set.

Expect.description:
What the answer has to be.

A status is a claim about the network path rather than about the service: Docker
publishes a port by putting a proxy in front of it, and that proxy accepts a
connection before knowing whether anything inside is listening. So a status alone
is not evidence — except for a refusal or a redirect to HTTPS, answers no port proxy
produces.

**A key of the four key-wise constraints is a place rather than a name.** A plain
name is a top-level member, and one beginning with `/` is a JSON Pointer, extended
with a step that picks an entry of a list by a field it holds. A flat name was enough while every service answered a flat object, and the
only thing it could say about a service that nests its payload was that the envelope
was there — which is a probe that passes by observing that something replied.

body_starts_with.description: What the body must begin with, where it is not JSON.

content_type.description: A substring of the content type the answer was served as.

exit.description: The exit status a run must end with. Not sufficient alone.

json.description: Places the answer must carry, each with the exact value it must hold.

json_array_min.description:
The answer read as an array, with at least this many entries.

A catalogue is very often a list rather than an object, and none of the
object-shaped constraints can say anything about one.

json_at_least.description: Places the answer must carry, each with a number it must not be below.

json_has_keys.description: Places the answer must carry, whatever they hold.

json_is_absent.description:
The answer did not parse as JSON at all.

Which is what a service that serves its application shell for every path it does
not implement answers — and the reason a status alone proves nothing against
one: the shell comes back `200` whether the API behind it exists or not, so what
has to be said is that the body was *not* a document.

json_types.description: Places the answer must carry, each with the kind of value it must be.

status.description: The status the answer must carry.

stdout_starts_with.description: What a run's standard output must begin with.

Expected.description:
Exactly what a place must hold.

Three kinds and no nesting: a flag that must be set, a number that must match, or a
word. A value deeper than this is asking about a document rather than about a claim
— and where the thing worth asserting is deeper *in* the answer, the key reaches it
rather than the value growing to match.

ExpectedKind.description:
The kind of value a key must hold.

Five, and closed. A name outside them is one no runner could evaluate, and an
assertion nothing evaluates is a proof that silently checks less than it says —
which is worse than one that fails.

Named for what it is the kind *of*, rather than `Kind`, because this is published
and whoever generates from it flattens every definition into one scope. `Kind` is
the one name there a generator is certain to want for itself: every envelope this
contract describes is keyed by its `kind`, so the union of them is a `Kind` too, and
two of them in one module is a definition nothing can be compiled against.

Health.description: How to tell a service has started.

kind.description: Which kind of probe to use.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait before calling it unhealthy.

HealthKind.description: The kinds of health probe a service can declare.

oneOf.description: Fetch a path on the service's port.
Open a connection to the service's port.
Trust the container's own reported state.

PluginRequest.description:
What is asked, and where.

Three fields and no more, and the third is the one worth explaining. A service that
answers XML unless a caller asks for JSON cannot satisfy a capability whose probe
requires a JSON assertion, and until this field there was nowhere to ask: Plex
answers `text/xml` at every path, including the one its health probe uses, unless
the request carries `Accept: application/json`.

**It is one media type and not a header map, and the difference is the point.** A
probe declares who it is asked as, and `none` on every `guarded` probe has meant what
it says partly because nothing could be presented. A map of headers would make that a
convention a reviewer has to hold — any service may name its credential header
whatever it likes, so no list of refused names could ever be closed — where one named
field keeps it a property of the format. A probe still cannot present anything,
because there is nowhere to write it.

accept.description:
The one representation the answer is asked for, as a media type.

Absent where the service needs no asking, which is most of them.

path.description: The path on the service being asked.

varies.description:
Each place in the answer whose value the service makes afresh on every run, a JSON
Pointer into its JSON, to the RE2 shape the whole value there is held to wherever a
recording is taken again. Never sent.

PluginRun.description: A run of the image's own program, as a proof declares it.

args.description:
Each argument handed to the image's entrypoint, one string each: one to 64, each at
most 4096 bytes and none holding a NUL.

timeout_s.description: How long the run may take, from 1 to 120 seconds. Default 30.

PluginShape.description: A privileged shape lemonfiber writes for a service.

oneOf.description: The host's render devices and the group that owns them.

RecordedWith.description:
What a recording gives a service in the operator's place: a constant reaching no third
party, or, written `"minted"`, a value made for that run alone.

Secret.description: A value a service holds, declared before anything captures or enters it.

carried_from.description: Where the service a part moves in place of wrote this credential itself.

for.description: The capability of the plugin's own that a credential crossing to it is needed to fill.

id.description: What the value is, within its namespace.

lapses_s.description:
How many seconds the value holds once an outside account issues it, for a code a
part is claimed with: lemonfiber asks the operator for it only to claim the part, and
keeps it no longer than the claim or this.

minted.description:
Whether lemonfiber makes the value at install, rather than anything capturing or
entering it, and in what shape.

needs.description: The values of other settings under which it is asked for and held.

recorded_with.description:
What a recording gives the service in the operator's place, where only the
operator holds the value and the service needs one to start.

was.description:
The variable an earlier release kept its value under in the stack's environment
file.

SecretCarriedFrom.description:
Where a service wrote a credential itself: a file inside its container, the format it
is written in and the dotted path to the value.

file.description:
The file, as a path inside the service's container beneath its configuration
directory.

format.description: The format the file is written in.

key.description: The dotted path to the value in the file; for `ini`, its section and entry.

SecretFormat.description: A format a service writes its configuration in.

SecretMinted.description: How a manifest writes [`Minted`]: `true` or `false`, or the shape it is made in.

anyOf.description: Made as a key, or not made.

SecretMintedShape.description: A shape a minted value is made in, beyond a key.

oneOf.description: A password: every character class a password rule asks for.
An email address at the plugin's own `.invalid` domain.

asks_for.description:
What it asks for out there, in the same terms.

Declared with [`Self::reaches`] or not at all: one without the other is half
an answer, and validation refuses it by name rather than quietly using the
half that is there.

bind.description: Which interface the port is published on.

certificate.description: The certificate lemonfiber makes for it before it first starts.

claim.description:
The evidence for what [`Self::provides`] names: one claim per capability, each
binding the capability's probes to requests on this service and to recordings.

Kept as the tables the stack wrote rather than read here. A claim is the plugin
contract's shape and that contract's reader is what holds it, so a bundled
service and a plugin standing in for it meet one set of binding rules; a second
reader here would be a second answer to what a claim may say, and this crate
cannot reach the first, which reads this one.

config_path.description:
Where inside the container its one configuration directory is mounted,
`/config` where absent.

config_ro.description: Whether its configuration directory is mounted read-only.

dashboard.description:
Its entry on the household's dashboard, as the plugin the bundle assembles it
from wires it. A stack directory's service declares none.

describes.description: What it does for the operator.

digest.description:
The digest of the image's multi-architecture index, `sha256:` and 64 lower-case
hex digits.

What actually runs. A digest names one index for good, where the tag beside it
could be moved to a different one tomorrow, so the stack resolves every image by
this and a service without one is refused by validation. Optional here so that
refusal can name the service, rather than the file failing to parse.

env.description: Its environment, each variable one of four typed kinds of value.

grants.description:
Extra kernel capabilities granted to the container, checked against an allow-list.

Named `grants` rather than `capabilities` because the word is about to mean
something else entirely: what a service *can do*, which is how a plugin declares
itself and how wiring asks for a filler. Two meanings under one spelling is how a
setting that decides what a container may do to the kernel gets read as a
description of what it offers.

The old spelling is still accepted, because an operator's own stack description is
theirs and a rename is not a reason to refuse to read it.

health.description: How to tell the service has actually started.

host_managed.description: True where the OS owns the lifecycle rather than Compose.

id.description: Unique, and matches the Compose service name.

last_release.description: The latest release upstream has published, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

listens.description:
The port it answers on inside the stack's network, where lemonfiber and the
services that ask for what it provides reach it.

Not always the port it publishes: `SABnzbd` publishes 8085 and answers on 8080.
Declared rather than known, so a service standing in for another is reached at
the port it answers on rather than at the one the service it replaced did.

mem_limit_mib.description: The most memory the container may hold, in MiB.

memory_mib.description:
The memory it expects to need, in MiB.

The stack's estimate, and only ever shown as one: a form's footprint is the sum
of these over the services it would start, and a figure read as a measurement
is one an operator believes and acts on. Optional because a stack that says
nothing has not said zero, and the services that are silent are named beside
the sum rather than counted as costing nothing.

mount.description: Each further path mounted from its own mount tree.

network.description: The capability whose filler's network it runs inside.

port.description: Primary UI or API port, absent for services with no listener.

posture.description: How tightly the container is held.

provides.description:
What this service can be asked for, as named capabilities.

An open list of strings here and checked for shape only, deliberately. The
published vocabulary is the set these names come from, and it is generated from
this field — a reader that held the set as well would be a cycle, and one that
held a copy of it would be a second answer to what the vocabulary carries. The
generator refuses a name the vocabulary does not carry, by name.

publish.description: Each further port it publishes on its tier.

reaches.description:
Where this service's own requests go, in the terms an operator would
recognise — not in protocol names.

An empty string is an answer: this service reaches nothing. That is not the
same as the field being absent, which is the stack declining to say, and the
two must never be read as one — an inventory of what leaves a machine that
rendered "we were not told" as "nothing leaves" would be making a privacy
claim out of its own ignorance.

Optional because a stack written before this existed says nothing, and a build
that refused such a manifest would refuse the stack it ships with. Where it is
absent, lemonfiber answers from what it knows about the services it ships, and
reports that it knows nothing where it does not.

rebuilt.description:
Paths beneath its configuration directory it rebuilds when they are missing,
which every backup leaves out.

secret.description:
The values it holds, each declared by the plugin the bundle assembles it from and
held in its own id's namespace. A stack directory's service declares none.

shape.description: The one privileged shape lemonfiber writes for it, from a closed set.

shares_config.description:
Where inside an adapter the whole configuration directory of the service it
fronts is mounted.

tag.description:
Explicit version — a floating tag is a validation failure.

The version an operator reads, and nothing more: a tag is a label its publisher
can move to another image, so what runs is named by [`Self::digest`].

takes_data.description: Whether it takes the data mount.

tmpfs.description: Absolute paths given scratch space in memory.

without_it.description: The consequence of not running it.

ServiceCertificate.description: The certificate lemonfiber makes for a service before it first starts.

certificate.description: Where the certificate is written, relative to the configuration directory.

key.description: Where its private key is written, relative to the configuration directory.

names.description: The host names it is made out to.

ServiceConstant.description: A value written exactly as declared.

ServiceIdVariables.description: The two variables an image reads the operator's uid and gid from.

gid_env.description: The variable it reads the operator's gid from.

uid_env.description: The variable it reads the operator's uid from.

ServiceMount.description: A further path mounted from the service's own mount tree.

from.description: The relative path inside the mount tree.

to.description: The absolute path inside the container.

ServiceNetwork.description: The network a service runs inside instead of its own: its filler's, or a fence's.

fenced.description:
Whether it fetches whatever address it is handed, and so runs inside a fence that
refuses every private address.

via.description: The capability whose filler's network it runs inside.

ServicePosture.description: How tightly the container is held.

oneOf.description: Six kernel capabilities, no privilege gained, a bounded process count.
A read-only root and no kernel capability at all, besides.

ServicePublish.description: A further port a service publishes on its tier.

listens.description: Where it answers inside the container, `port` where absent.

port.description: Where it is published on the host.

ServiceSetting.description: An operator setting, with what is written while none is recorded.

default.description: What is written while the operator has recorded no value.

needs.description: The values of other settings under which it is written.

one_of.description: The values its service accepts, where it says.

recorded_with.description:
What a recording gives the service in the operator's place, where only the
operator holds the value and the service needs one to start.

was.description:
The variable an earlier release kept its value under in the stack's environment
file.

ServiceUrlOf.description: The address of a capability's filler.

files.description: The medium the filler asked for files.

native.description: The upstream's own API, where the ask reaches the upstream an adapter fronts.

ServiceUserMode.description:
How a manifest writes [`UserMode`]: a mode by name, or the variables an image reads
the operator's ids from.

anyOf.description: The variables its image reads the operator's uid and gid from.

ServiceUserModeName.description: A user mode a manifest writes by name.

oneOf.description: The operator's uid and gid as the container's user.

anyOf.description: A value that is always a choice.
Values that are choices only where `needs` is met.

SettingChoiceNeeding.description:
Values that are choices only where the other settings `needs` names hold one of the
values it lists.
